subject: Urgent: ACME Health - sustained p95/p99 regressions, request backlog
messages:
From: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@acmehealth.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: ACME Health Platform Team <platform@acmehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Jun 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: API latency — severe p95/p99 regressions since 13:00 PDT

Hi Laura,

We started seeing sustained p95 and p99 regressions and a large number of 502/503 errors for our hosted API traffic starting ~13:00 PDT. Throughput looks healthy on our side but requests are queuing and tail latency is spiking — our Observability shows queue depth growing from median 2 -> 48 over 30 minutes. This is impacting user flows for two key features.

Attached a screenshot from our Grafana and a CSV snapshot of queued requests. Can you confirm this is on Redwood’s side? We need an ETA for mitigation — this is blocking our production rollout tomorrow.

Thanks,
Oliver
Oliver Grant
Head of Platform, ACME Health

Thanks for the data, Oliver — we’re on it.

Short version: I’m escalating to Ops and Eng. Sean/Dylan, can you triage ASAP and confirm whether this is queue/backpressure on our hosted fleet (batching or queue depth) or an upstream model issue? Please share immediate mitigations (routing, throttles, model fallback) and an ETA for rollback or fix.

Oliver — I’ll update every 30 minutes until resolved and follow up with a timeline for credits if this meets our SLA threshold.

Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference
From: dylan_brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, sean_gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Jun 2026 15:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: API latency — initial triage (queue depth suspected)

Laura / Sean — initial triage notes:

- Observed matching p95/p99 spikes across the US-hosted pool for the model variant serving ACME traffic.
- Request backlog shows long-tail queuing inside our batcher when kernel-selection for longer contexts coincided with a sudden burst of medium-size requests.
- Autoscaler did not scale up fast enough due to a conservative cooldown (configured per-customer).
- Error patterns: transient 502s consistent with overloaded inference workers dropping requests once local batch queues exceed threshold.

Immediate mitigations I propose (ordered by speed):
1) Bypass batching for ACME’s route (switch to eager mode) — tradeoff: higher per-token cost, much lower tail latency.
2) Increase per-customer concurrency cap + force scale-up to spare nodes in the US pool.
3) Route overflow to a compatible lighter-weight model variant (quantized 8-bit) while we stabilize.

I’ll run a config change to toggle eager-mode and bump concurrency. Rolling change will take ~6–8 minutes to observe. Preparing rollback plan now.

— Dylan
From: sean_gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, dylan_brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, hannah_schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Jun 2026 15:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: API latency — mitigation in progress

Update: enacted mitigation #1 and #2 at 15:40 PDT. Quick notes:
- Switched ACME route to eager mode (batching disabled) and bumped their concurrency cap from 8 -> 24.
- Triggered scale-up in US-hosted pool; new nodes started joining; some model shards warmed from cache.
- Observed immediate drop in p95 after ~3 minutes, but p99 still elevated — long tails persist.
- Telemetry link: https://grafana.redwood.local/d/ops/acme-health-requests?from=now-1h

Next steps: if p99 remains high after 15 minutes, we will route excess traffic to the quantized variant (w/ slight latency improvement and reduced throughput pressure). Requesting authorization to automatically failover if no improvement by 16:05 PDT.

— Sean
From: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: hannah_schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, dylan_brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, sean_gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Jun 2026 16:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Executive brief — ACME Health outage risk and customer impact

Hannah / Marissa — FYI and requesting exec-level clearance:

Summary: ACME Health (strategic mid-market customer, annual committed spend ≈ $420k) experienced severe tail-latency starting 13:00 PDT. We have enacted immediate mitigations (eager-mode + increased concurrency + scale-up). p95 improved significantly; p99 remains elevated. If p99 does not normalize by 16:05 PDT, ops will failover their traffic to a lighter model variant (quantized) which will reduce tail latency but may have small quality diffs.

Risks:
- Customer has a production rollout tomorrow; this could jeopardize go-live.
- Potential SLA credit exposure and executive escalation to ACME leadership if we don’t resolve quickly.

Ask: authorize automatic failover to the quantized variant at 16:05 PDT if p99 > 2x baseline, and approve starting the SLA remediation process. I’ll take point on communications.

– Laura
From: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@acmehealth.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: ACME Health Platform Team <platform@acmehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Jun 2026 09:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: API latency — update from ACME; improved but want RCA

Laura,

Thanks for the rapid response — we saw p95/p99 move back to acceptable ranges after the eager-mode and scale-up changes; failover to quantized variant wasn't necessary. The incident window lasted ~2.5 hours and did impact a small percentage of end-users.

Next steps on our side: we’d like a post-incident RCA that explains what caused the batching/backpressure mismatch, confirmation of permanent config changes to avoid recurrence, and a proposed credit for the impacted window per our contract. Can you get that to us within 72 hours?

Appreciate the quick coordination.

Oliver
